clue.text: Approved bringing in teacher with sense

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: having good sense, thinking straight

indicators.note: the word for approved takes the teacher's word into its middle

parts.note: cleared means approved, given the go-ahead
a head is a head teacher

explanation.surface: A school inspector signs off a new teacher who seems to have good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thinking lucidly and rationally is described as having sense, with a mind free of confusion.

clue.text: Sock or socks (inter alia)?

definitions.meaning: to sock is to hit hard, punch
socks among other garments: gear, clothing in slang

explanation.surface: A question of which item of hosiery is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word both for striking someone and for one's clothes and belongings.

clue.text: Anaesthetic? I will avoid indication of options

indicators.note: the options word keeps clear of the letter I, which is dropped

parts.note: either introduces a choice between options

explanation.surface: An anaesthetist refuses to offer the patient a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile liquid was one of the earliest general anaesthetics; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: I rush downhill, perhaps cutting through railway, taking a chance

indicators.note: the I and the downhill word cut into the railway abbreviation

parts.note: to ski is, for example, to rush down a slope

explanation.surface: A skier speeds down a slope across a railway line, gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a hazardous, gambling manner is to act while running a risk.

clue.text: Liking to give off soft charm

indicators.note: the liking word gives off, or emits, the soft letter

parts.note: a penchant is a liking or fondness
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A fondness that radiates gentle charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight or captivate them, as if by a spell.

clue.text: Trifling group, united in support of Democrat

definitions.note: a noun use: idle flirting or toying, not the adjective

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits below the Democrat

parts.note: an alliance is a group united for a common cause

explanation.surface: An unimportant coalition backs a Democratic politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifling' looks like an adjective (trivial) but is the noun: flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual flirtation or playing with an idea is called trifling, a light-hearted involvement.

clue.text: Compound Greek character inscribed in semiconductor

indicators.note: the Greek letter is written inside the semiconductor word

parts.note: a diode is a semiconductor device
xi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek letter etched into a silicon chip.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon or sulphur combined with two oxygen atoms forms this kind of chemical compound.

clue.text: Costume article appearing in finale? Not quite

indicators.note: the article shows up inside the shortened word for the finale
not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the close is the end or finale of something
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A costume item turns up in the last act of a show, though not quite at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final E of the finale word before 'appearing in' places the article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Costume is a general word for garments worn, so it stands for what one wears generally.

clue.text: Education, possibly, is a special extended case

definitions.meaning: read whimsically: what happens in a classroom lesson, activity in class
a lawsuit brought on behalf of a large group of claimants

explanation.surface: Someone argues that schooling is a matter for an unusually long trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit by many claimants is literally activity in a class, which teaching also is.

clue.text: Hard time avoiding requests for assistance?

indicators.note: the requests' word does without the time abbreviation, which is taken out

parts.note: callouts are requests for help, as for a plumber or emergency service

explanation.surface: A tough period in which someone avoided answering pleas for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard in the sense of unfeeling or hard-hearted, insensitive to others' suffering.

clue.text: What may provoke anger with s/h typo?

definitions.text: What may provoke anger with s/h typo?

indicators.note: provoke is read as stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: s/h is a written abbreviation for shorthand

explanation.surface: A shorthand error may make someone angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may provoke' stirs ANGER, SH and TYPO; and the whole clue says shorthand writing could cause such a typo to annoy someone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the art of writing in shorthand, so a shorthand typo belongs to it.

clue.text: Inclination to offload first gem

indicators.note: the word for inclination unloads its first letter

parts.note: camber is the slight slope or inclination of a road surface

explanation.surface: Someone feels inclined to get rid of their first jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMBER loses its first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised tree resin of a yellow-orange colour is used in jewellery and counted as a gem.

clue.text: Stress? It is apparent in book's heroine

definitions.note: a verb: to emphasise, here by typeface, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the second word shows up inside the heroine's name

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A reader asks about the stress that is evident in a novel's leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' suggests pronunciation or worry; here it is emphasis by typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting words in slanted type is a printed way of giving them emphasis, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Increase limits of radiotherapy for operation

parts.note: a surge is a sudden increase

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A doctor raises the intensity of radiation treatment before an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical procedure is commonly called an operation, and the place doctors work is also called this.

clue.text: Eastern statue, perhaps, last of all to obscure Northern payment

indicators.note: the last letter replaces, covering up, the N

parts.note: a statue is an example of a monument

indicators.note: the final letter of all is taken

explanation.surface: An oriental statue blocks a view of the north, last of all.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the last of 'all', replaces the first N in MONUMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Salary or fees received for work count as remuneration, a formal word for payment.

clue.text: New set probing aspect of Chinese philosophy will bear fruit

indicators.note: the new-and-set pair goes into the philosophy word as a probe enters

parts.note: the Tao, the Way, is central to Chinese philosophy
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Fresh thinkers studying Chinese philosophy will be productive.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Credit left will secure a home extension?

indicators.note: the credit abbreviation holds the A inside it

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A homeowner leaves a loan in place to pay for an extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shelter for a vehicle is often built against the side of a house, a sort of add-on.

clue.text: Sport — motor-racing — that's embraced by supporter becoming rowdy

definitions.note: a noun here: a rough, noisy person

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: the motor-racing piece is held within the supporter word

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
F1 is Formula One motor racing, written FI

explanation.surface: A rugby or motor-racing fan turns into a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: Formula One's F1 is written with I for the digit; 'that's embraced by' puts it inside the supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowdy, as a noun, is a violent or disorderly person, a thug or hooligan.

clue.text: Fabric factory no longer ready, needing additional year

parts.note: ready is cash; a tanner was an old sixpence coin, money no longer in use

explanation.surface: A textile mill is not yet ready and needs another year.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was a pre-decimal British sixpence; 'ready' is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hides are turned into leather, a material, at this kind of works.

clue.text: Carbon leads to more efficient detergent

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
leaner means more efficient, with less waste

explanation.surface: A chemist says carbon makes a washing agent work better.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a substance used for washing things clean, an agent of cleaning.

clue.text: Marine creature, animal without a scale

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish

indicators.note: the animal word goes without the letter A

parts.note: a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: A sea creature, a fish without scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like a fish's scale; it is the verb, to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or cliff is to climb it awkwardly, using hands and feet.

clue.text: Cut devastating figure in New York, in smart style

indicators.note: the shortened figure sits within the New York abbreviation
the figure's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Attila the Hun ravaged much of Europe

explanation.surface: A striking person makes an impression in New York, dressed smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' drops the Hun's final A, and 'in' sets the remainder inside the city abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something neatly and fashionably, dapper in dress, is done in a smart way.

clue.text: Popular mix of fun and zeal is something very infectious

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A winning combination of fun and enthusiasm proves contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link; 'mix of' rearranges the letters of the two words either side to give FLUENZA.
explanation.definitionFit: The flu is a highly contagious viral illness, passed readily from person to person.

clue.text: Ridiculed nameless organisation

indicators.note: without a name, so the abbreviation N for name goes

parts.note: sent up means mocked or ridiculed

explanation.surface: An anonymous group was mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: The way an organisation or system is arranged is its structure or arrangement, a common noun use.

clue.text: Brushed last of dirt under tipped-up seats

indicators.note: in a down answer, the final letter comes below
in a down answer, the seats word is turned upside down

parts.note: pews are church seats

indicators.note: the final letter of dirt is taken

explanation.surface: The last of the dirt was swept under folding seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped-up' turns PEWS into SWEP, with T below.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaned with a broom or lightly touched in passing, both senses of the past tense.

clue.text: Simple attitude shown by excellent sort of doctor in Tyneside area

indicators.note: the excellent sort and the doctor sit within the area abbreviation

parts.note: NE is the North East of England, where Tyneside lies
A1 means first-rate, written AI
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A first-rate animal doctor in north-east England shows an uncomplicated outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, 'excellent', is written with the letter I standing for the digit one.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence and lack of worldliness, a guileless outlook, is what this word for unsophistication names.

clue.text: Economy? British Minister heading off financial centre

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

indicators.note: the financial centre loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Questions about the economy as a British minister leaves for the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips the C from CITY to leave ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy of words means conciseness, so the question mark signals this sense of shortness.

clue.text: Determined to follow with eggs in essence

indicators.note: the determined word comes after the other

parts.note: nits are lice eggs, so nitty means full of them
gritty means showing grit, determined

explanation.surface: A resolute person comes after those carrying eggs, at the heart of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic, essential details of a matter are its core facts, the real substance.
